q: Why did my sales drop yesterday?

checks.what: tool: measures the change with compare_period

answer:
Sales did not fall yesterday versus the day before — net sales were ₹91,220 on 2026-10-13, up 127.4% from ₹40,119 on 2026-10-12. Versus the system’s “usual” day the level was 12.0% lower (usual = ₹103,283), but that difference is within normal day-to-day variation and the diagnosis found no supported causal driver.

What changed (ordered by impact)
- Volume and price both rose: Orders 26 → 45 (+73.1%) and Net AOV ₹1,543 → ₹2,027 (+31.3%) — together they explain the jump from ₹40,119 to ₹91,220.  
- Component shifts: Gross sales fell vs the usual (₹111,567 → ₹102,961, -₹8,605 effect) and discounts were higher (₹3,349 → ₹5,173, -₹1,824 effect) — these moved net sales versus the usual baseline but did not create an unusual one-day event.  
- Return / cancel revenue was much lower than usual (₹17,414 → ₹1,601, a −₹15,813 effect on gross sales), which is the largest arithmetic contributor to the difference from the usual level.  
- Campaign/ad signals to review: one ad (TH-471-PLAYSCRATCHLOUNGE_IMG_6516) appeared with ₹24,962 and several TH-383 campaign ads dropped to zero; these are notable shifts but the data cannot prove they caused the net-sales movement.

Worth checking: review the two campaigns/ads named above and the unusually low return/cancel revenue on 2026-10-13 to see if operational timing or reporting explain the “usual” gap.
